title: British Columbia arms: a visual catalogue
subtitle: 32 illustrated specimens, proposals, objects and reproduction treatments
scope: A bounded survey of variants found in accessible public sources and the supplied document crops. Specimen count is not a count of official redesigns.
datePolicy: Design/adoption dates, object dates, report periods, imprint years, artwork dates, image publication and retrieval dates are separate. An attested use is not an introduction date.
readingKey: Dates distinguish a design from the object or publication showing it. Drawing-family names describe visible features; they are not official version names. Undated artwork stays undated. Source scans, paper colours and SAMPLE watermarks are retained. Images are scaled independently for comparison.

entries.title: Vancouver Island colonial seal
entries.description: Royal Arms sit above a separate device with a beaver and crossed implements. This belongs to the predecessor colony, before the provincial sun-and-waves arms.
entries.datingNote: Dispatch dated 29 June 1850; photograph dated 18 April 2016.

entries.title: Lion, crown and B/C badge
entries.description: Crowned lion and crown, B/C letters and a leafy wreath. The provincial shield and supporters are absent.
entries.datingNote: Governor’s flag approved 9 July 1870. This drawing is a later reproduction; its original date is unknown.

entries.title: Lorne’s four trial shields
entries.description: One sheet contains four alternatives with crosses, saltires and feline figures. These form a separate, unadopted branch of the design history.
entries.datingNote: LAC dates the sheet c. 1882; the older printed caption says 1881. Official metadata takes precedence.
entries.credit: LAC/PAC · MIKAN 3922080 · e010767157 · older ref. C16216

entries.title: Crest, branches and motto
entries.description: Branches and a broad motto ribbon surround the lion and crown. There are no B/C letters, provincial shield or animal supporters.
entries.datingNote: The suggested c. 1890–1896 range is tentative. The illustration’s publication in 2012 is secure.

entries.title: Beanlands arms: line drawing
entries.description: Sun and waves occupy the upper shield; the Union Flag fills the lower field. Stag, ram, royal crest and motto complete the composition.
entries.datingNote: Adopted 19 July 1895. This web illustration is not dated original artwork; the asset filename “1890” is misleading.

entries.title: Great Seal with the older shield
entries.description: The Beanlands composition is enclosed by a circular inscription. Relief, border and compressed proportions distinguish this specimen from the printed drawing.
entries.datingNote: Sources disagree on the September introduction day; catalogue the year only. Seal use reportedly extended to 1911.

entries.title: Diamond Jubilee stained glass
entries.description: The older shield is rendered in glass, with the motto wrapped around it and the supporters integrated into the window’s ornament.
entries.datingNote: The Legislature dates the commissioned window to the 1897 Diamond Jubilee. It preserves the 1895 design family.
entries.credit: Photograph: Legislative Assembly of British Columbia

entries.title: Speaker’s Chair carving
entries.description: The arms become a wooden relief: broad antlers, rounded supporters and deep scrollwork. The shield retains the original sun-above-flag arrangement.
entries.datingNote: Official history dates the chair and canopy to the 1890s and credits Muirhead & Mann; the precise carving year is not established.

entries.title: Foley China pin dish
entries.description: A coloured rendering of the older shield, slender supporters and scroll appears above a small British Columbia caption.
entries.datingNote: Foley China (Wileman & Co.). The object’s manufacture date is unverified; this is separate from the reported 1906 Wedgwood plate.
entries.credit: Vachon Collection, Canadian Museum of Civilisation
entries.transformation: Original embedded JPEG extracted without resampling

entries.title: Museum title page
entries.description: Low crown and long projecting scroll tails, with a condensed government caption. The small scan suggests the same broad family as 1935.
entries.datingNote: The scan is too soft to establish an identical printing block.
entries.imprintEvidence: PDF page 1 imprint: Victoria, B.C.; William H. Cullin, Printer to the King’s Most Excellent Majesty; 1916.
entries.confidence: Moderate: same broad arrangement as the clearer 1935 report, but this small scan is too soft to certify identical printing block.
entries.transformation: PDF page rendered directly with PyMuPDF; crop only. No retouching, tracing or generated replacement. Scan quality and ink density can affect apparent line weight.

entries.title: Fine engraved museum arms
entries.description: Low, open-looking crown; slender supporters; narrow shield and long forked ribbon tails. Fine hatching differs visibly from later bold blocks.
entries.datingNote: A dated use of this drawing; its introduction date and artist are unknown.
entries.imprintEvidence: PDF page 1 imprint: Victoria, B.C.; Charles F. Banfield, Printer to the King’s Most Excellent Majesty; 1936.
entries.confidence: High for visible low-crown/long-scroll design; no claim of a formally named official version.
entries.transformation: PDF page rendered directly with PyMuPDF; crop only. No retouching, tracing or generated replacement. Scan quality and ink density can affect apparent line weight.

entries.title: Canada Year Book drawing
entries.description: A larger, long-bodied lion, high rounded crown, fuller supporters and curled scroll ends distinguish this drawing from the museum engravings.
entries.datingNote: Contemporary commentary describes the crest and supporters as established through usage.
entries.imprintEvidence: 1943–44 edition identified by Statistics Canada archive URL; this extracted single-page plate has no visible printed page number or separate imprint.

entries.title: Blue museum cover arms
entries.description: Domed crown, bold Union-cross, upright supporters and long forked ribbon tails. The single blue ink is a printing colourway.
entries.datingNote: The dated report documents use, not a new grant or adoption.
entries.imprintEvidence: PDF page 29 bottom imprint: Victoria, B.C.; Don McDiarmid, Printer to the Queen’s Most Excellent Majesty; 1953. Director’s letter on PDF page 4 is dated February 2nd, 1953.

entries.title: Brown museum cover arms
entries.description: A clearer example of the domed-crown, long-scroll family in brown ink. Compare the shield, crown and supporter outlines with the 1952 specimen.
entries.datingNote: Broad family match; identical master or printing block not established.
entries.imprintEvidence: PDF page 36 bottom imprint: A. Sutton, Printer to the Queen’s Most Excellent Majesty in right of the Province of British Columbia; 1961. Director’s letter on PDF page 4 is dated January 16th, 1961.

entries.title: Government history illustration
entries.description: The Union Flag and small antique crown now occupy the top of the shield, with waves and sun below. The earlier crest and supporters remain.
entries.datingNote: The website’s “1906” label identifies the design phase. This full achievement is not a scan of the 1906 warrant.

entries.title: Alternative colour illustration
entries.description: A broad crown and lion, differently modelled supporters, pointed shield and red-edged scroll distinguish this published colour rendering.
entries.datingNote: No original drawing date established. Its placement beside a warrant transcription does not make the image a warrant scan.

entries.title: Split serif heading
entries.description: British and Columbia flank the old arms in serif capitals. The number below belongs to the document, not the arms.
entries.datingNote: User-supplied crop. No date or full archival record is available.

entries.title: Government-caption heading
entries.description: Old arms above the condensed government caption, followed by order number 1121 and an approval line.
entries.datingNote: The complete OIC was independently retrieved; its first page confirms the heading and approval date. The engraving date remains unknown.

entries.description: Blackletter heading on the Kootenay District map attachment for Provincial Rental Housing Corporation, Crown Grant No. 8498.
entries.datingNote: The complete OIC confirms this occurrence. The map creation date and original grant issue date remain unknown.

documentaryRecordsAndLeads.title: Shield granted in 1906
documentaryRecordsAndLeads.status: Documentary evidence; exact original image not retrieved
documentaryRecordsAndLeads.details: A shield-only painting by Henry W. Gray reproduced in Swan's 1977 book and The Blazon Summer2021 p.6; original painting date not established

limitations: The catalogue is not exhaustive of every drawing, seal impression, printer block or decorative object.
Three pre-1987 drawing families are visual groupings; no master-artwork or block identity is claimed.
No original 1906 warrant image or exact master for the supplied document crops was recovered.
The Blazon Winter 2012 has chronology errors, including a 1997 caption for the 1987 arms and an incorrect ceremony location. Primary sources take precedence.
Sources disagree on 6 versus 16 September 1896 for the seal. The catalogue uses 1896 only.
The original date of the foliage-and-motto badge is unresolved.
The provincial 1895 GIF and de Vries grayscale image appear to reproduce the same drawing family; the latter is listed as an alternate source, not counted twice.
Reference imagery is not presented as newly drawn export artwork; source credits and watermarks remain.
